name: Shobi
title: David's Warrior and Servant
summary: Shobi, son of Nahash from Rabbah in Ammon, was one of those who came to David's aid when he fled from his son Absalom. He brought supplies and food to David and his people while they were exhausted in the wilderness. Shobi represents a remarkable Ammonite ally who showed loyalty to King David during a difficult time.

keyEvents.title: David's Flight from Absalom
keyEvents.description: When David fled from his son Absalom's rebellion, he had to leave Jerusalem and go out into the wilderness with his faithful servants.

keyEvents.title: Shobi Brings Supplies to David
keyEvents.description: Shobi, son of Nahash from Rabbah in Ammon, was one of three men who brought beds, basins, earthen vessels, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, butter, sheep, and cheese to David and his people at Mahanaim.

keyEvents.title: David's Arrival at Mahanaim
keyEvents.description: David and his people arrived at Mahanaim, where they were met by Shobi and other allies who provided for them because they were hungry, tired, and thirsty after traveling through the wilderness.

keyEvents.title: Ammonite Connection with David
keyEvents.description: Shobi's father Nahash apparently had a friendly relationship with David, which may explain Shobi's loyalty. This stands in contrast to his brother Hanun, who had insulted David's messengers.

keyEvents.title: Allies Gather Around David
keyEvents.description: Together with Makir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar and the Gileadite Barzillai from Rogelim, Shobi formed a group of loyal supporters who helped David in his darkest hour.
